domain: Apple Silicon / Industrial Design / Hardware Criticism

slides.headline: $1,999 Still Doesn’t Buy Apple’s Best
slides.subheadline: Faster silicon, familiar hardware, and a mandatory storage upgrade complicate the entry-level Pro.

slides.headline: New Silicon Inside A Familiar Shell
slides.subheadline: The design dates to 2021. The M6 brings more cores and active cooling.

cards.title: 12 CPU cores
cards.body: Two top-performance super cores, four performance cores, and six high-efficiency cores.

cards.title: Ports, both sides
cards.body: Three Thunderbolt 4 ports, MagSafe, HDMI, headphone jack, and SD card reader.

cards.title: Sustained workloads
cards.body: Active cooling fans; USB-C charging from either side.

slides.headline: The Entry Price Keeps Climbing
slides.subheadline: Historical comparisons expose the creep. The optional matte display costs extra.

tiers.label: Increase over M5’s original starting price
tiers.body: Compared with the starting price from a year ago.

tiers.label: Increase over basic M1 MacBook Pro
tiers.body: Compared with the basic model from 2020.

tiers.label: Optional nano-texture matte finish
tiers.body: Not included in the $1,999 starting price.

slides.headline: Graphics Gains Outrun The CPU Bump
slides.subheadline: The reviewed 16GB M6 model improves on M5, with larger gains over M3.

metrics.label: GPU versus M5, depending on test

slides.headline: The Pro’s Case Against The Air
slides.subheadline: Display, connectivity, and cooling distinguish the Pro—not a dramatically different keyboard or trackpad.

sides.title: M6 MacBook Pro
points: 14.2 inches; Mini LED with local dimming; 120 Hz ProMotion.
Maximum SDR brightness: 1,000 nits. HDR brightness: up to 1,600 nits.
Active cooling, more ports, and a thicker, heavier chassis.

sides.title: 13- and 15-inch MacBook Air
points: Fanless, thinner, and lighter, with fewer ports.
Historically throttles sooner; keyboard and trackpad are broadly comparable.

slides.headline: Mandatory Storage, Conditional Memory Bandwidth
slides.subheadline: Storage is fixed at entry. Memory capacity determines bandwidth, while flagship display features remain absent.

cards.title: Storage you cannot decline
cards.body: The mandatory 1TB allotment applies even when you do not need it.

cards.title: Memory upgrades
cards.body: 24GB and 32GB configurations receive 170 GB/s memory bandwidth.

cards.title: Missing flagship features
cards.body: The retained 2021 design offers neither an OLED panel nor a touchscreen.

slides.headline: Good Laptop. Awkward Position.
slides.quote: this isn’t a bad laptop, but it is an awkwardly positioned one.
slides.subheadline: The reviewer questions whether the Pro delivers $500 to $700 more value than the Air.

slides.headline: Your Current Mac Changes The Verdict
slides.subheadline: Older machines strengthen the upgrade case. Recent owners face a less compelling performance jump.

cards.title: Consider: M1 or M2 owners
cards.body: Air or Pro users should notice a sizable day-to-day upgrade, according to the reviewer.

cards.title: Hold: M4 or M5 owners
cards.body: The reviewer expects noticeable gains, but nothing staggeringly large.

cards.title: Consider: sustained workloads
cards.body: Active cooling and additional ports strengthen the case against a fanless Air.

cards.title: Reconsider: flagship-screen shoppers
cards.body: At $1,999, this model still lacks OLED and touch.

slides.headline: Don’t Buy On An Unconfirmed Roadmap
slides.subheadline: The review’s future-facing claims are conditional, rumored, or explicitly speculative—not Apple commitments.

cards.title: M6 MacBook Air
cards.body: Discussed conditionally, not as a confirmed release.

cards.title: M6 chip family
cards.body: The absence of Pro, Max, or Ultra configurations is presented as rumor.

cards.title: OLED touchscreen timing
cards.body: The reviewer speculates a wait of at least two years; Apple has not committed.

cards.title: Component constraints
cards.body: The reviewer cites ongoing RAM and storage shortages as reasons normal progression is uncertain.

slides.headline: Buy The Benefits, Not The Badge
slides.subheadline: Choose this Pro for its display, ports, and sustained performance—not for Apple’s newest design.

cards.title: The strongest fit
cards.body: Buyers seeking Apple’s cheapest laptop with 120 Hz ProMotion or optional $150 nano-texture.

cards.title: The weakest fit
cards.body: Buyers who do not need mandatory 1TB storage or expect OLED and touch.

slides.cta: Are those Pro benefits worth $1,999 to you?
